subject: Fail to factorize Q - point process model

messages.author: 1426e25bcb2cd4e9
messages.subject: Fail to factorize Q - point process model
parts:
Hello,

I am new to INLA and having some trouble with my model and I would really apricate any help! I am running a point process model using prediction, estimate and integration stacks. When I run the model I get the below error over and over, but it does eventually run. I've read previous threads about adding prec.intercept but this does not make any difference. My covariates are all scaled. Any help greatly apricated! See my code for the model formulation below. Many thanks, Melissa

file: smtp-taucs.c  eabef9f0c5191d7287b59145b03d23ae93e5728b - Sat May 7 11:06:00 2022 +0300
    Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 725, Thread: 0
    Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

form <- resp~ 0 + intercept + cov1.s + cov2.s + cov3.s +
  cov4.s + cov5.s + cov6.s  + cov7.s +
  cov8.s +
  f(spatial.field, model =pcspde)

fixed_mean = 0
fixed_precision = 0.001
fixedprior <- list(mean= fixed_mean, prec = fixed_precision)

mod1 <- inla(form, family = 'poisson', control.family = list(link='log'),
             data=inla.stack.data(integrated_stack),
             control.fixed = fixedprior,
             control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(integrated_stack), link =NULL, compute =TRUE),
             E = inla.stack.data(integrated_stack)$e,
             verbose = TRUE,
             control.compute = list(waic = FALSE, dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE))

it could be the model is only weakly indentifiable and more informative
priors, like for the fixed effects will help. If these msg's are there
in the beginning of the fit (run with verbose=T), then its ok.

If I need to rerun it here, I need a complete example
